profile.summary: UTR-LM is a language model for the 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) of mRNA, the stretch before the coding sequence that strongly affects how well an mRNA is translated. It reads a 5' UTR sequence and, after fine-tuning, predicts mean ribosome loading, translation efficiency or mRNA expression level. Pretraining combines masked language modelling with labels computed from the sequence, such as secondary structure and minimum free energy.

summary_quotes.text: Specifically, the 5' UTR, located at the 5' end of an RNA molecule, is a critical determinant of the RNA’s translation efficiency.
We augmented the model with supervised information that can be computed given the sequence, including the secondary structure and minimum free energy, which improved the semantic representation.
The model outperformed the best-known benchmark by up to 42% for predicting the Mean Ribosome Loading, and by up to 60% for predicting the Translation Efficiency and the mRNA Expression Level.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: UTR-LM is built on a modified copy of the ESM-2 transformer code, shipped in the repository. Each nucleotide is a token, a [CLS] token is added, and tokens become 128-dimensional vectors fed to six transformer layers with 16 attention heads. Pretraining masks 15% of nucleotides and reconstructs them (masked nucleotide task). Two optional supervised tasks use labels computed with ViennaRNA: predicting the secondary-structure symbol at masked positions, and predicting the minimum free energy (MFE) from the [CLS] representation with a two-layer feed-forward predictor. For downstream tasks the developers replace the MFE target with the task label and fine-tune the whole model, using a Huber loss in the README's commands. In the paper, the MRL model used the downstream library, secondary structure and MFE in pretraining, and the TE and EL models used the downstream library and MFE. Training ran on four V100-SXM2 16 GB GPUs on AWS and four P100 PCIe GPUs on a Stanford cluster, for at most 200 epochs and two days.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository holds 16 pretrained checkpoint files under Model/Pretrained, named by their pretraining variant (ESM2, ESM2SI, ESM2SS, ESM2SISS, ESM2DSD) and data split, plus 179 checkpoint files under Model/Downstream: 178 for the TE and EL tasks and one for MRL (fold 0 of a single library). The README's own example pretraining command passes --heads 6 --embed_dim 16, which disagrees with the 16 heads and embedding size 128 listed under General Parameters and in the checkpoint file names. A result should name the exact checkpoint file and the repository commit. A runnable copy is also published as a CodeOcean capsule.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Semi-supervised masked language model for 5' UTR sequences, fine-tuned for regression tasks (mean ribosome loading, translation efficiency and expression level). The paper also adapts it to classify internal ribosome entry sites (IRES) with a contrastive loss.

quotes.text: # UTR-LM: A Semi-supervised 5’ UTR Language Model for mRNA Translation and Expression Prediction
- label_type: Choose from "te_log" (TE task) or "rnaseq_log" (EL task)
- huber_loss: We use HuberLoss. If not choose, it will use MSELoss.
for predicting the Mean Ribosome Loading, and by up to 60% for predicting the Translation Efficiency and the mRNA Expression Level
We adopted a contrastive learning approach to distinguish between IRES and non-IRES.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer based on modified ESM-2 code. The paper describes an encoder of six transformer layers with 16 attention heads and 128-dimensional token embeddings, with layer normalisation and residual connections, followed by a two-layer feed-forward predictor block that reads the [CLS] token. The README's General Parameters and the checkpoint names give the same 6 layers, 16 heads and embedding size 128.

The encoder block consists of a six-layer transformer
These tokens are first converted into 128-dimensional vectors via an embedding layer
The predictor block is a two-layer feed-forward neural network.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: 5' UTR nucleotide sequences, one token per nucleotide plus a [CLS] token, supplied as FASTA for pretraining and as CSV files for fine-tuning. The TE and EL example uses an input length of 100, matching the paper's fixed 100-bp length for those tasks; the MRL libraries are 50-nucleotide 5' UTRs.

facts.value: Predicted mean ribosome loading (MRL), translation efficiency (TE) or mRNA expression level (EL); embeddings and attention can be extracted with the prediction notebook. In the paper the model is also fine-tuned to classify IRES and to predict luciferase relative light units (RLU).

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The paper's pretraining corpus: 214,349 5' UTRs from Ensembl across five species (human, rat, mouse, chicken and zebrafish), eight synthetic libraries of random 50-nucleotide 5' UTRs from Sample et al., and three endogenous human 5' UTR datasets analysed by Cao et al. (HEK, PC3 and Muscle), plus unlabelled sequences from the downstream task datasets. The pretraining file named in the README holds 255,795 sequences with energy and structure labels; the paper's 214,349 refers to the Ensembl part only, and the sources do not say exactly which parts make up the README file.

strengths.text: Pretrained checkpoints and fine-tuned TE and EL checkpoints are committed in the repository, so these runs do not need a separate weights download; only one fine-tuned MRL checkpoint is included.

strengths.text: Pretraining can add labels computed from the sequence itself (minimum free energy, secondary structure). The README says this improved the representation. The paper is more mixed: for MRL the variants differed only slightly, while for TE adding the downstream library and the MFE loss gave substantially higher performance and adding secondary structure could lower it.

run_guide.summary: Set up the UTR-LM environment with its modified ESM code, then fine-tune a pretrained checkpoint for translation efficiency on the Muscle cell line.
prerequisites: Conda, and a CUDA GPU: the commands launch torch.distributed and set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
Task data downloaded by hand from the Google Drive folder linked in the README (for the TE and EL task, the Muscle, pc3 or HEK cell-line data).
Paths in the commands changed to your own directories, as the README states.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/a96123155/UTR-LM.git
cd UTR-LM
git checkout --detach b77b589bf182eb9de6a1a5024fa09d44294d94fc
steps.explanation: The README does not give a clone command; this clones the repository named in the README and pins the commit read for this page. Later commands are run from the repository root.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Install step 2 and Instruction Example

quotes.text: In UTRLM environment, install the Python packages listed in the utrlm_requirements.txt file.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n UTRLM python==3.9.13
conda activate UTRLM
pip install -r utrlm_requirements.txt
steps.explanation: The README's environment steps. The requirements file pins a full conda environment including local build paths, so the plain pip list in the README may be needed instead.

steps.title: Install the modified ESM code
steps.shell:
pip install fair-esm
find -name esm
scp -r ./Scripts/esm ./.conda/envs/UTRLM/lib/python3.9/site-packages/
steps.explanation: Installs fair-esm, then copies the repository's modified esm folder over it. The destination path must match your own environment.

steps.title: Fine-tune for translation efficiency
steps.shell:
cd ./Scripts/UTRLM_downstream
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -m torch.distributed.launch --nproc_per_node=1 --master_port 9001 MJ4_Finetune_extract_append_predictor_CellLine_10fold-lr-huber-DDP.py --device_ids 0 --cell_line Muscle --label_type te_log --seq_type utr --inp_len 100 --huber_loss --modelfile ./Model/ESM2SI_3.1_fiveSpeciesCao_6layers_16heads_128embedsize_4096batchToks_MLMLossMin.pkl --finetune --bos_emb --lr 1e-2 --dropout3 0.2 --epochs 300 --prefix TE_ESM2SI_3.1.1e-2.M.dropout2
steps.explanation: The README's TE and EL command for the Muscle cell line, using the ESM2SI_3.1 pretrained checkpoint. Change --cell_line to pc3 or HEK, and --label_type to rnaseq_log for the expression-level task. The README's --modelfile path does not match the repository tree: there is no Model folder under Scripts/UTRLM_downstream, and the checkpoint is at Model/Pretrained/ESM2SI_3.1_fiveSpeciesCao_6layers_16heads_128embedsize_4096batchToks_MLMLossMin.pkl. From Scripts/UTRLM_downstream, pass ../../Model/Pretrained/ESM2SI_3.1_fiveSpeciesCao_6layers_16heads_128embedsize_4096batchToks_MLMLossMin.pkl instead.
steps.source_locator: README.md: 2. For TE and EL task; GitHub tree listing, Model/Pretrained

outputs: Fine-tuning logs and a trained predictor checkpoint for the chosen cell line and label type. The README does not state the output paths; the prediction notebook MJ5_Predict_and_Extract_Attention_Embedding.ipynb reads such a checkpoint to produce predictions, embeddings and attention.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The checkpoint path in the README's TE command is ./Model/ESM2SI_3.1_... while the repository stores that file under Model/Pretrained/, so the path needs adjusting.
Data must be fetched by hand from Google Drive, with no checksum.

notes: Code and weights are GPL-3.0, so the README, LICENSE and requirements bytes are hashed and not stored. The paper's full text is now saved as the PubMed Central XML of the NIH author manuscript; its licence element allows text mining and fair use only, so store_bytes is false and no licence is recorded on the source. The README's example pretraining flags (--heads 6 --embed_dim 16) contradict its own documented settings and the paper (16 heads, 128 embedding size); worth a human look before anyone follows that command. The README and the paper name different CodeOcean capsules. The bioRxiv API response gives the preprint licence as cc_no, which is not a reuse licence, so its source carries no licence field; the GitHub tree response states no licence.
